title: Opening an SVG file gives you its drawing to edit
goal: Someone who builds icons will try to open an existing SVG in Photonz, from File Open or from the Finder, and today it appears to do nothing: the app does not even list itself for SVG files in the Finder. Find out exactly what happens, then make opening an SVG give a document holding its drawing at its own size, the way a picture opens.
notes: From the rough list of queue/audits/2026-10-16-svg-logo.json: 'Opening an SVG with no document open (Finder > Open With) still does nothing; only bringing one into an open document is covered.' NOT reproduced by the manager, hence p2 and the first checklist item. Evidence it is likely: the built probe's Info.plist CFBundleDocumentTypes lists png/jpeg/tiff/heic/gif, recordings and the Photonz document, no public.svg-image (plutil -p 'dist/Photonz Probe.app/Contents/Info.plist'). File Open allows [.image, photonzType] (Sources/Photonz/AppCoordinator.swift:992-1001) and .svg conforms to public.image, so File Open probably lists SVGs and then openWindow(.file(url)) tries to load it as a bitmap. Library import already keeps an SVG as VectorArt (Sources/Photonz/EditorState+LibraryImport.swift:20-25, 115-130): reuse that, do not write a second SVG reader. Whether the drawing should come in as editable shapes rather than one vector layer is a later question; one sharp vector layer is enough here. Info.plist source lives with Scripts/build-app.sh.
acceptance: Reproduced first, with the exact steps and what happened pasted into this task's log: File Open on an .svg, a .svg dropped on the app's icon, and Open With from the Finder
Opening an SVG from File Open, or dropping one on the app icon, opens a new document sized to the SVG's own canvas with its drawing on a layer, sharp at every zoom
The app is listed for SVG files in the Finder's Open With menu (as an alternate, never taking over the default)
A file macOS cannot draw (an .svgz, a broken SVG) says so in a plain message instead of doing nothing

Try path, no flag changed from Next defaults: File, Open, pick an icon SVG; audit written under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: from ask-draws-a-dog (2026-10-20): Sources/PhotonzCore/SVGArtwork.swift now reads an SVG into editable layers (paths with every command and arcs, circles/ellipses as ovals, rects, polygons, groups with transforms, fill rules, style attributes, a gradient's first colour) and SVGArtwork.group(named:fitting:) makes them one group; all 992 Twemoji drawings read. Opening an SVG as a document could build on it.
digest 2026-11-05: raised from p2 to p1. The user made icons the focus today (icon-svg), and focus work outranks everything.

Reproduced 2026-11-06 on the probe at 1869c67d, fixture /tmp/svgrepro/arrow.svg (24x24 stroke icon). (1) File Open: the panel's allowed types are [.image, photonz] and UTType.svg conforms to .image, so SVGs are listed and pickable; picking one goes openFileWindow -> .file(url) -> openImageOrSidecar -> openImage, where CGImageSourceCreateImageAtIndex returns nil for an SVG (standalone check printed 'arrow.svg CGImageSource: true type: nil image: nil NSImage: (24.0, 24.0)') and the guard returns with no message. A walk with one open step on that exact door printed: '[1 open] FAILED: an editor for arrow.svg did not appear within 15.0s'. The panel itself could not be driven unmanned; the walk's open step hands the same .file id the panel does. (2) Dropped on the app icon: the Dock only takes files the app declares, and Info.plist declares no public.svg-image, so the icon refuses it; the same open-documents event sent with 'Scripts/probe-app.sh <file>' (open -a) left one 1240x900 window with no document and no message (CGWindowList, one layer 0 window; a real Dock drag cannot be made here, Ghoztty Accessibility denied). (3) Open With: NSWorkspace.urlsForApplications(toOpen:) on arrow.svg listed Edge, Chrome, Safari, VS Code, TextEdit, Notes, Image Playground and no Photonz. Also: arrow.svgz and a truncated broken.svg both give NSImage nil, and .svgz is public.svg-image too, so both are pickable and fail the same silent way.

Chose editable shapes over the one vector layer the notes settled for, because the title says to edit and the reader could do it; one sharp picture stays as the fallback when shapes would lose part of a file. Chose an Icon picture at 512 for a 24 unit file over a literal 24 point canvas, because Viewport.fit never enlarges; the file still writes 24 by 24. Chose the white blank canvas under the drawing, as New Icon has, because Export leaves it out by default and dark ink on the dark window would be unreadable. Chose Viewer plus Alternate in Info.plist: measured with NSWorkspace, Editor+Alternate made the probe the default for .svg over Edge, None dropped it from Open With, Viewer+Alternate lists it and Edge stays default.
